chapter: Chapter 8. Enterprise Risk Management and Future Trends
stem: An ERM manager at a large financial institution is meeting with a risk consultant on the subject of improving the firm’s risk culture framework. The risk consultant uses examples to describe the elements of a strong risk culture. Which of the following is appropriate for the consultant to mention as an example?
stem_short: Which is an example of a strong risk culture?

stem_highlights.text: elements of a strong risk culture

options.A: A compensation plan that is developed based on the business structure of a startup company in the industry
options.B: A weekly firm-wide meeting in which managers of each business unit report their work progress
options.C: A company culture that encourages resolutions of risk control violations to be made exclusively within business units
options.D: A flexible risk management style that more easily accommodates activities that are likely to result in a profit

high.label: GOOD INDICATOR
high.text: Risk information flows up and across the firm
high.at: One sign of a strong risk culture

A.reason: Pay should fit your own risk appetite, not a startup's structure.

C.reason: Violations should escalate, e.g. via whistle-blowing — not stay in units.

D.reason: Bending rules for profit invites too much risk.

takeaway.text: Risk info flows up and across

sections.text: [warmly] Hey, welcome back to Risk Hub! FRM Part 1, Book 1, Foundations of Risk Management. Chapter 8, Enterprise Risk Management and Future Trends. Let's do a practice question.

So, an ERM manager at a large financial institution is meeting a risk consultant to improve the firm's risk culture. The consultant uses examples to describe a strong risk culture. Which of these is a good example to mention?

Option A. A compensation plan based on the business structure of a startup in the industry. Option B. A weekly firm-wide meeting where the manager of each business unit reports on their progress. Option C. A culture where risk control violations are resolved only within business units. And option D. A flexible risk management style that more easily allows activities likely to make a profit.
Okay, pause the video and lock in your answer. [long pause]

[excited] And the answer is... B! [warmly] Here's why. One sign of a strong risk culture is how risk information flows. In a weekly firm-wide meeting, every business unit reports, so information flows up and across the firm. That helps capture and highlight enterprise-scale risks.

Now, why not the others? A is wrong. Compensation should support your own firm's risk appetite and culture, not copy a startup at a different stage. C is wrong too. Violations shouldn't stay hidden in business units. Staff should know how to escalate, for example through whistle-blowing. And D? Bending the rules for profit lets in too much risk. A strong culture penalizes risk violations, even when they make money.

[warmly] So, the key takeaway. Risk information should flow up and across the firm. Pay should match the firm's risk appetite. And violations get escalated and penalized, even when they're profitable. If this helped, follow Risk Hub for more FRM practice. See you in the next one!
